title: Sourdough
summary: A hydration number, a flour, and a complaint about your oven. That is the entire first conversation and it renews.

larp.dek: The knowledge is free, the practice is slow, and nobody is going to ask you to produce a loaf tonight.

crib.heading: References
lines: Hydration as a percentage. The whole hobby is spoken in percentages.
Tartine is the shared text. Forkish is the other one.
Bulk ferment, shaping, cold retard. The three stages.
Banneton, lame, dutch oven. The three objects.

crib.heading: Opinions to hold
lines: Starter age is a joke, not a credential.
Open crumb is overrated and mostly hydration.
The oven matters less than the shaping.

phrases.when: Asked how the baking is going. Every baker's starter sulks.

phrases.line: That's a high hydration, isn't it?
phrases.when: Shown a loaf with an open crumb. Correct often enough, and it is the right axis.

phrases.line: I under-proof more than I over-proof.
phrases.when: Asked what goes wrong. Naming your own recurring failure is the mark of a baker.

surface: A hydration number, a flour, and a complaint about your oven. That is the entire first conversation and it renews.
Nothing about this scene happens on a deadline, which is why the clock is long.

follow_up.question: "Can I see it?"
follow_up.why: Everyone photographs the crumb. Having no photograph is the only real failure state, and it is recoverable within a week.

counter.move: Show a loaf that went wrong. Bakers trust failure more than crumb shots, and a dense one with a theory about why is a stronger answer than a perfect photograph with none.
counter.holds: Indefinitely. The whole scene is built on comparing failures.

tells: You talk about the starter and not the schedule. The schedule is the hobby.
You have no complaint. Every baker has one recurring failure they are mid-argument with.
cost: None. The worst outcome is that somebody gives you starter, which is a gift and an obligation.
You will be asked about it in three weeks. That is the only follow-up.

learn.make: Six loaves. The fourth is where it starts working.
